free_tier.stated: no free tier: the README requires "Cloudflare account (Workers paid plan, $5/mo)"

egress.terms: not applicable; the Worker plan is priced per month, not per byte, and the README states no transfer figure; ingress: tcp

interface_detail: wrangler deploy plus a 12 MB Go bridge
tooling: Go bridge plus pnpm and wrangler; a CA certificate must be installed on each device
chaining: composes with a Cloudflare account and a paid Workers plan, and with cloudflare-tunnel only if the Worker is fronted by one.

limits.value: no figure stated; the Workers paid plan is billed per request and duration beyond the included allowance

binding_note: the Worker sits in the data path and every datagram becomes Worker work, so the plan's request and duration billing is what fails first at sustained volume; the README states no figure for it

identity_cost.detail: a Cloudflare account on the Workers paid plan at $5/mo, which needs a payment method

reliability_note: the Worker terminates and re-originates TLS, so every upstream connection is intercepted by design; single maintainer, no releases
confidence_note: a probe through a deployed Worker would raise it, and would also be the only measurement of a Workers-hosted WireGuard path in this corpus

evidence.proved: "Cloudflare account (Workers paid plan, $5/mo)" in the prerequisites
the architecture line: stock WireGuard client, Go bridge over a single WebSocket, Durable Object, TLS MITM, then fetch() upstream
2 stars, no releases, last push 2026-04-06; the description calls it "Very rough"

price_per_tb_month: USD 5 per month, Workers paid plan
notes: This is the only wrapper that moves the far end off a host the client runs and onto a hosted service, and it is the reason the structural fact is worth stating precisely: replacing the far host with a Worker costs $5/mo and adds a TLS-intercepting proxy in the path, so it is a paid answer to a paid problem, not a free path. Two stars and no releases means it is a design sketch, not a deployment.

extras.wg_detail: device runs a stock WireGuard client against localhost:51820, a Go bridge (wireguard-go plus gvisor netstack) forwards over one WebSocket to a Cloudflare Durable Object
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the Worker plan is priced per month, not per byte, and the README states no transfer figure
extras.transit_note: through a Cloudflare Durable Object, which sees the plaintext of every intercepted connection
extras.hosting_requirement: no host of the client's own, but a Cloudflare Workers paid plan at $5/mo, and a device able to run the Go bridge
